props.title: Set It Off
props.initialSlug: Four women risk it all in desperate bank heist

sections.content: Set It Off revolutionized the heist genre by centering Black women's experiences and economic struggles. Director F. Gary Gray crafted a gritty, emotional thriller that went beyond typical crime film tropes to explore systemic inequality, female friendship, and desperate choices. The powerhouse ensemble of Jada Pinkett Smith, Queen Latifah, Vivica A. Fox, and Kimberly Elise brought raw authenticity to their roles as working-class women driven to rob banks. This film paved the way for later female-led crime dramas like Widows (2018) and helped establish Gray as a major director before his work on Friday (1995) and Straight Outta Compton (2015).

sections.content: The mid-1990s marked a crucial period for Black cinema, with Set It Off emerging alongside powerful works like Higher Learning (1995) and Eve's Bayou (1997). These films moved beyond the male-dominated narratives of the early '90s hood films, offering complex portrayals of Black women's experiences. The film's exploration of institutional racism, police brutality, and economic disparity remains painfully relevant, while its action sequences rival any mainstream heist thriller of the era.

Queen Latifah's portrayal of Cleo was groundbreaking as one of the first openly lesbian Black characters in mainstream cinema. This representation, while not the film's central focus, added crucial dimension to the story and helped pave the way for more diverse LGBTQ+ characters in Black cinema, influencing later works like Pariah (2011) and Moonlight (2016). sections.content: Set It Off challenged Hollywood's traditional heist formula by grounding its action in social realism. Unlike glossy capers like Ocean's Eleven (2001), the film portrayed crime as a last resort for marginalized women failed by the system. This influenced later socially-conscious crime films like Hell or High Water (2016) and Hustlers (2019), which similarly explore economic desperation as a catalyst for crime.
